headline: Chicago scrap still expected up $10–$40 a ton in November
detail: BL Duke sees all grades rising, with mills trying to hold it to $10–$30 and busheling futures above $500. The settle should land by about Nov 10, and mills running harder this week help the dealer side.

headline: Copper slides again Tuesday as AI stocks sell off
detail: After closing near $6.54 Monday, COMEX fell to about $6.30–$6.40 overnight as chip stocks dropped and China moved to slow the yuan. Expect yards to mark copper down if this holds.

headline: Copper scrap bounces 9 cents; steel scrap flat
detail: ScrapMonster lifted top copper grades 9¢/lb and most brass 2¢ on Monday after a 14¢ drop Friday. Aluminum and all steel grades held, and most stainless slipped a penny. Tuesday’s copper drop could erase the gain.

headline: US mills ran at 88.9% last week, up sharply
detail: Raw steel output jumped 15.7% in a week to 2.053 million tons, which Steel Market Update says is the most since August 2008. Busier mills need more scrap heading into the November settle.

headline: US hot-rolled reaches $1,434; Nucor spot goes to $1,280
detail: Midwest HRC rose $5 Monday, up about 9% in a month, and Nucor raised its spot price $10 for a 15th straight week. Buyers in a new survey expect more increases into year-end.

headline: Gold and silver rebound as oil plunges
detail: Gold rose 1.8% to about $3,946 and silver about 3% to $50.50 Monday as cheaper oil eased inflation fears. Both gave some back early Tuesday, with gold near $3,920.

headline: Oil drops 8% on Iran talks, then bounces on new strike
detail: Brent fell to $104.77 Monday on signs of renewed US-Iran talks, then rose to about $106.62 after a reported US strike on Qeshm Island. Energy is what drives smelter costs and Fed hike bets right now.

headline: LME copper stocks jump nearly 20,000 tons
detail: Warehouse stocks rose 19,775 tons in a day to 293,775, and the official cash price slipped to $14,380. A build that size weighs on prices even with mine supply tight.

headline: US factories beat forecasts; Fed hike odds near 75%
detail: The ISM index rose to 55.5 with production at its best since 2021, and aluminum and copper were listed as still in short supply. Strong demand helps metals, but it keeps a December hike likely.

headline: Lutnick is restarting Canada tariff talks
detail: Formal talks may resume this week, with earlier progress on lowering steel duties under a quota and cutting aluminum duties; autos remain the hard part. A deal could cool US steel and aluminum premiums.

headline: China’s factory surveys split; stocks and yuan in focus
detail: The official PMI fell to 49.3 while the private one held at 52.0, and the CSI 300 lost 8.5% in October. The central bank also started daily overnight operations at 1.25%. Weak official demand keeps steel and iron ore capped.

headline: Chile slashes 2026 copper output forecast by 8.4%
detail: Cochilco now sees 4.94 million tons this year and only a small rebound in 2027, with September output down about 15%. That is the main floor under copper during the tech selloff.

headline: China pays a record premium for copper
detail: Its import premium topped $200 a ton, the highest in Fastmarkets data since 2017, as Chinese stocks fell over 25% to about 54,000 tons. Tight China supply is the bulls’ best argument against the selloff.

headline: Palladium drops to its lowest since June 2025
detail: Prices fell to about $947 early Tuesday, down about 20% in a month, on fund outflows and weak auto demand. Falling palladium means lower payouts on catalytic converters.

headline: Platinum near a one-year low around $1,435
detail: The drop follows fund outflows and higher rate bets, and the World Platinum Investment Council now sees a 265,000-ounce surplus in 2026. Rhodium quotes have not moved, so converter values are leaning on the other two.

headline: Turkish scrap holds firm near $400
detail: Kallanish reported a fresh US deal holding prices firm, and BL Duke says Turkey is approaching $400. Export strength supports HMS and other obsolete grades here.

headline: China scrap prices fall across aluminum and copper
detail: Every aluminum grade fell 150–300 yuan a ton Monday and top copper grades fell 200 yuan. Softer Chinese buying can pull on export scrap values.

headline: U.S. Steel breaks ground on $1.9 billion Arkansas iron plant
detail: The direct-reduced iron plant will feed the Big River electric furnaces with Minnesota ore. It could trim purchased prime scrap in time, though the company has not said how much.

headline: Iron ore steadies above $91 as China output dip disappoints bears
detail: China’s daily hot metal fell just 0.2% to about 2.32 million tons, a smaller drop than feared, and the benchmark rose to $91.25. Goldman still sees about $88 by year-end.

headline: USW and U.S. Steel still far apart on a contract
detail: Talks resumed in person last week, but the sides remain well apart more than two months past the deadline. A strike at Gary or other mills would hit scrap demand.

headline: Drought cuts an Indonesian nickel plant to 30%
detail: Nickel Industries’ ENC plant dropped from about 50% of capacity until rains expected in December, and CRU trimmed its 2026 output forecast for this nickel feed. It gives some support to a market still in surplus.

headline: North American aluminum demand up 3.5% as imports fill the gap
detail: Domestic shipments fell 3.6% in the first half while imports, mostly sheet, covered the rise. The industry is now pushing for more recycling, which favors scrap buyers.

headline: US aluminum premium at a record as Canadian metal goes to Europe
detail: The 50% US tariff on Canadian aluminum has pushed US prices to a record gap over world prices. That keeps US scrap aluminum values supported, unless the Canada talks change it.

headline: Data centers keep nonresidential building growing
detail: Nonresidential spending rose 0.6% in September, its sixth straight gain, with data centers up 8.6%. Without data centers and power, spending fell. That is steady copper and steel demand from one narrow source.

headline: Housing starts fell 5.2% in September
detail: Starts dropped to a 1.22 million pace and single-family permits fell 4%. Weaker home building trims demand for copper wire and pipe, aluminum and steel.

headline: Ford lifts its 2026 metal cost estimate to about $2.5 billion
detail: The increase from about $2 billion cites copper and steel, among other costs. Automakers are feeling high metal prices and may push suppliers harder.

headline: October US car sales seen at a 16.1 million pace
detail: Cox Automotive expected about 1.38 million sales, up 7.2% from a year ago with an extra selling day. Steady sales mean steady stamping scrap and demand for sheet steel.

headline: Refined copper tariff still undecided
detail: The White House has not ruled on a proposed 15% tariff from January 2027, and US-held stocks are expected to stay put until it is dropped. That keeps COMEX and LME prices apart.

headline: Nasdaq 100 falls into a correction
detail: It dropped 1.4% Monday as investors questioned AI spending, while the 10-year yield closed at 4.91%. A fading AI story hits copper and tin hardest.
